tweets.text:
On 3/25, at the USBP checkpoint in Westmorland, CA, a sharp-nosed USBP K9 went to work and sniffed out a major meth load stashed in a floor compartment. USBP agents uncovered 22 foil-wrapped packages packed with +114 lbs. of the dangerous drug. The U.S. citizen driver didn’t get far—agents handed both the driver and the seized drugs over to the DEA. Now, that driver is facing serious charges for possession with intent to distribute (21 USC 841). 
 
Another example that checkpoints work.

tweets.text:
Last week, at the Javier Vega Jr. Checkpoint in Kingsville, TX, Border Patrol agents arrested a Cuban national with a troubling criminal history.

Agents discovered that he had a felony conviction for cruelty toward a child and had previously lost his U.S. residency. His employment authorization was expired, and he had no lawful status to be in the country. He now faces charges as an inadmissible alien (8 U.S.C. § 1182) and for reentry after removal/entry without admission (INA 212(a)(9)(C)(ii)).
